theory.title: Вопросы к подлежащему
theory.text: Если вопросительное слово (who, what, which, how many) само является подлежащим, вспомогательный глагол не нужен, и порядок слов прямой.

head: Вопрос к дополнению
Вопрос к подлежащему
rows: Who did you call? (ты звонил кому-то)

theory.title: Косвенные вопросы
theory.text: Косвенные вопросы звучат вежливее. После вводной фразы (Could you tell me…, Do you know…, I wonder…) порядок слов становится прямым, а do/does/did исчезают. Если вопрос был «да/нет», используем if или whether.

examples.en: Where is the station? → Could you tell me where the station is?
What time does it start? → Do you know what time it starts?
Did he accept? → I wonder if he accepted.

theory.tip: Вопросительный знак ставится только если вводная фраза сама вопрос (Do you know…?). После I wonder… — точка.

exercises.title: The art of the job interview question
exercises.text:
Most candidates prepare answers for a job interview, but far fewer prepare questions. That's a mistake, say recruiters. When an interviewer asks 'Do you have any questions for us?', replying 'No, I think you've covered everything' can suggest a lack of curiosity.

The best questions are specific and show that you've done your research. Instead of asking what the company does, you might ask how a recent change has affected the team. It's also wise to avoid asking about holidays or salary in a first interview — not because these things don't matter, but because the timing can make you seem more interested in the benefits than in the job itself.

Finally, recruiters suggest one question that almost always impresses: 'What would success look like in this role after six months?'

questions.statement: Most candidates prepare questions for the interviewer.

questions.question: Saying you have no questions can suggest…
Why avoid asking about salary in a first interview?
options: It can make you seem more interested in benefits

questions.text: The recommended question is about success after ___ months.

exercises.title: A difficult customer

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: Excuse me, could you tell me why my order hasn't arrived yet? It was supposed to be here on Monday.

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you know what your order number is?

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: Yes, it's four eight one five two.

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: Thank you. It looks like the courier tried to deliver it on Tuesday, but nobody was home.

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: Well, I wonder why nobody called me. Who decided not to leave it with a neighbour?

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: I understand. I'll arrange a new delivery for tomorrow morning, free of charge.

questions.question: The order should have arrived on…

questions.statement: The courier didn't try to deliver it.

theory.title: Вспомогательные глаголы: зачем они нужны

head: Функция
Пример
rows: Did you like it? — Yes, I did.
I've been to Peru. — Have you? Wow!
I'm tired. — So am I. / I can't swim. — Neither can I.
I love jazz. — Really? I don't.
I DO like your dress! / She DID call, I promise.

theory.tip: Вспомогательный глагол в реакции повторяет время исходной фразы: I went → So did I; I've finished → So have I.

theory.title: the … the … + сравнительная степень
theory.text: Конструкция «чем…, тем…»: обе части начинаются с the + сравнительная степень.

examples.en: The more you practise, the better you get.
examples.ru: Чем больше практикуешься, тем лучше получается.

examples.en: The sooner we leave, the earlier we'll arrive.
examples.ru: Чем раньше выйдем, тем раньше приедем.

examples.en: The older I get, the less I worry.
examples.ru: Чем старше я становлюсь, тем меньше переживаю.

items.text: I love horror films. — Really? I ___. I hate them.
She's never been to Italy. — Neither ___ I.
I didn't enjoy the concert. — Didn't you? I ___!
I can't swim. — Can't you? I thought you ___.

items.prompt: If you practise more, you get better.
answers: The more you practise, the better you get.

items.prompt: If you leave earlier, you'll arrive sooner.
answers: The earlier you leave, the sooner you'll arrive.
The earlier you leave, the sooner you arrive.

answers: The darker it gets, the colder it gets.
The darker it gets, the colder it becomes.

exercises.title: Why do we interrupt?
exercises.text:
We often think of interrupting as rude, but linguists say the picture is more complicated. In many conversations, short interruptions such as 'Do you?', 'Really?' or 'So did I!' are actually signs of engagement. Researchers call this 'cooperative overlap': the listener isn't trying to take over, but to show interest.

The problem arises when people from different conversational cultures meet. A speaker who expects silence while they talk may feel constantly cut off, while a speaker who uses overlap may interpret silence as boredom. The more aware we are of these differences, the less likely we are to misjudge each other.

questions.statement: All interruptions are rude, according to linguists.

questions.question: A speaker who uses overlap may think silence means…

questions.text: The more aware we are, the ___ likely we are to misjudge each other.
